title: Priority decay & safety throttles for dedicated→hosted spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a robust priority-decay scoring and safety-throttle layer that governs when requests are allowed to spill over from Dedicated capacity to Hosted. Primary goals: protect customers' reserved capacity SLAs, minimize inadvertent cost/exposure when upstream capacity is constrained, and provide predictable availability behaviors with observable fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Priority score computed for every request (tenant, route, model, region) with configurable decay parameters exposed via Console
When Dedicated capacity is saturated, only requests with current priority >= configured threshold are eligible for spillover
Global and per-region safety throttles enforce an upper bound on percent of traffic spilling to Hosted (default 8%)
Circuit-breaker closes spillover for a tenant if hosted error rate or latency exceed configured SLOs for more than 2 minutes
Metrics emitted for priority distribution, spillover rate, throttle hit-rate, and per-tenant circuit-breaker state
E2E tests cover normal saturation, burst spikes, slow-hosted degradation, and gradual decay of priority
implementation_notes: Priority components: base_tier_weight (enterprise/pro), route_criticality, short-term SLA_penalty, time_decay(t) with half-life configurable (default 30m)
Scoring formula (pseudocode): score = clamp(base_tier_weight * route_criticality - sla_penalty) * exp(-ln(2) * elapsed_minutes / half_life)
Safety throttles implemented as token-bucket per-region and a global elastic budget backed by Redis to support cross-pod enforcement
Circuit-breaker uses rolling window (2m) of error-rate + p50 latency; tripped state stored in service KV with TTL and exposed via tracing
Config surfaced in Console under 'Routing Policies' with per-customer overrides and an API for programmatic changes
Feature-flag gated rollout: default off for all customers, opt-in for a subset of high-volume dedicated customers for 2-week canary
Telemetry: add metrics tags for tenant_id, tenant_tier, region, model_variant, route_name to allow post-incident attribution
tradeoffs: Strict throttles reduce availability for some requests but protect cost/SLA for tenants—balance configured via conservative defaults
Using Redis for global budgets simplifies enforcement but adds an operational dependency; alternative is eventual-consistent local budgets which risk brief over-spill
Complex scoring increases mental overhead for SEs, but provides fine-grained control needed for enterprise SLAs
Per-tenant overrides increase feature complexity and support surface; plan limited rollout and strong defaults to mitigate
qa_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and decay behavior across edge time windows
Integration tests simulating capacity exhaustion in a Dedicated pool and verifying spillover gating
Chaos test: induce progressive hosted latency and verify circuit-breaker and telemetry behave as expected
Load test with synthetic tenants to validate global throttle remains under configured percent during spikes
Manual validation with two pilot customers in different regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1)
release_notes: Adds priority-decay routing with per-region safety throttles to control Dedicated→Hosted spillover
Default conservative limits: 8% global spillover budget, half-life 30m, circuit-breaker on hosted error-rate >5%
Admin Console: new 'Routing Policies' section for inspecting and adjusting thresholds
Ops playbook: rollback flag, disable spillover globally via feature toggle in emergencies
